options: The tow overtakes the tug and passes it safely on one side
The towline drags the tug broadside and she cannot recover
The towline parts under load and the tow drifts away free
A tug turns in a small tight circle while towing astern
questions.explanation: Transport Canada's Ship Safety Bulletin 16/2020 describes girding as a towline pulling the tug broadside with the tug unable to recover, which can quickly capsize it. A parted line or a tight turn is not girding.

questions.stem: Which combination makes girding MORE likely?
options: A short towline, tug close to the tow, course or speed change, tow catching up
A long towline, the tug well clear of the tow, steady speed and a tow falling astern
A long towline, steady course and speed, and the winch clutch released
Calm weather, no current, and all hull openings closed and secured
questions.explanation: The bulletin lists a shortened towline (a steeper angle), a close tug, speed or course changes and a tow overtaking the tug among the risk factors. The other options describe the opposite conditions.

questions.stem: When may a tug tow with the winch clutch engaged, according to the bulletin?
options: Whenever the towline is under steady load
Only in calm weather with a light tow
Always, to stop the line paying out
Only while adjusting the towline length
questions.explanation: Transport Canada's bulletin says never tow with the winch clutch engaged except while adjusting the towline length. Letting the line pay out is part of avoiding girding; paying out more wire to freshen the nip on a long tow is a related precaution.

questions.stem: Which of these is part of the regular test of a tug's emergency release system?
options: Test it once a year at the wheelhouse control only, with no tow attached
Test it only when the tow is first connected, and never again after that
Test every release position, brake and clutch release, and reset
Test it by actually cutting the towline while the tow is connected
questions.explanation: The bulletin asks for regular tests that include every location of the abort system, that the winch brake and clutch release and that the system fully resets. Testing at one place or once only misses faults, and cutting a live tow is an emergency action, not a test.

questions.stem: Which item belongs in a master's tow plan?
options: The tug's colour scheme, radio call sign and crew uniform sizes only
Tug power and bollard pull against the tow, and connection plans
The tow's full cargo manifest, with nothing at all about the tug
The passenger lists of both the tug and the tow, signed by the master
questions.explanation: The bulletin's tow plan covers the tow's size and limits, tug power and bollard pull, the towing point and towline length, stability, connection and disconnection, the route and weather, and consumables. Passengers should not be aboard at all (s. 404(3)).

questions.stem: A passenger-carrying vessel under Part 4 of the Small Vessel Regulations is about to take a barge in tow. What must be true, except in an emergency?
options: No passengers on the vessel or tow, and she meets s. 521
Passengers may ride on the tow but not on the towing vessel itself
Passengers may stay on board if every one of them wears a lifejacket
There is no restriction as long as the barge is under 15 GT
questions.explanation: Section 404(3) says that except in an emergency the operator must ensure there are no passengers on the vessel or the tow and that the vessel meets s. 521. Lifejackets and tow size do not remove the restriction.

questions.stem: Which list matches the requirements of SVR s. 521 for a workboat that tows?
options: One lifejacket in the wheelhouse, a hand axe in the cabin, one way out, a bulwark aft of the tow point
Two lifejackets for every person on board, a fire pump, and a gob wire fitted at the stern
Two lifejackets in the wheelhouse only, a written tow plan, and a radar reflector on the mast
Lifejackets in wheelhouse and engine space, quick release, two exits, clear deck aft
questions.explanation: Section 521 lists the two lifejackets in the wheelhouse and two in the engine space if normally occupied, a means to release or cut the tow line immediately, two means of escape from the wheelhouse located so one is usable if heeled, and a clear deck aft so the line can swing freely.

questions.stem: An open (not decked) workboat is used for towing. Which SVR s. 521 requirement applies to her hull?
options: She must be fully watertight forward of the towing point
She must have a collision bulkhead and a full double bottom
Buoyancy when swamped, or a gunwale high enough
She must have no freeing ports anywhere in her bulwarks
questions.explanation: Section 521(f) says an open workboat must have positive buoyancy when swamped or a gunwale of adequate height. The watertight-aft-of-the-towing-point and rapid-drainage requirement is for decked vessels (s. 521(e)).

questions.stem: According to Transport Canada's tug guidance, how can the towline of a tug on a winch be dealt with in an emergency?
options: Only the deck crew at the stern can release it, using a ratchet
Release controls at each steering position, plus a cut or release at the bollard
The towline must be unshackled at the barge end before any release
No release is needed at all if the winch is hydraulically driven
questions.explanation: TP 15491 describes controls at each steering position to reduce tension or release a hook and a means to sever or release the line at the bollard, or a clearly marked axe. It also says a winch must not have a ratchet that prevents paying out.

questions.stem: A 9 GT tug designed and built for towing is fitted out for general towing work (not log salvage). What do the Navigation Safety Regulations, 2020 require under s. 121?
options: Two searchlights mounted to sweep 360 degrees together
One searchlight on the mast
No searchlights; they apply only to vessels over 150 GT
Two searchlights, but only if the tow exceeds 200 m
questions.explanation: Section 121 requires two searchlights on vessels designed and constructed to tow that are over 5 GT, unless they tow only to salvage logs, mounted to sweep 360 degrees together. The 200 m figure applies to the towing lights, not to searchlights.

questions.stem: A tug is towing a barge and the tow is more than 200 m long (measured as in the Rules). How is this shown?
options: Two masthead lights in a vertical line, and a ball by day
A single masthead light, and a cone point down by day
Three red lights in a vertical line, and two balls by day
Three masthead lights in a vertical line, and a diamond by day
questions.explanation: TP 15491 gives three masthead lights for a tow longer than 200 m, with a diamond by day (Rule 24). Two masthead lights is the arrangement for a shorter tow.

questions.stem: Which statement about girding in Canadian waters is supported by the TSB figures reported?
options: Girding has never once led to a capsizing in Canadian waters
There were 26 capsizings and 21 girding situations from 2005 to 2018
26 girding situations from 2005 to 2018 led to 21 capsizings
All girdings from 2005 to 2018 happened in the Strait of Georgia
questions.explanation: The TSB, in the report of the 2018 George H. Ledcor capsizing on the Fraser River, recorded 26 girding situations leading to 21 capsizings in 2005-2018. The other options reverse or invent figures.

questions.stem: A towing watch is posted on a tow. What does the Canadian Coast Guard's 1993 SAR guidance say about the watch?
options: The watch stays down in the engine room and never looks at the tow
The watch keeps eyes on the tow, with a cutting tool close by
The watch is needed only at night, when the tow is hard to see
The watch releases the tow whenever the speed changes at all
questions.explanation: TP 11637 designates a towing watch who constantly observes the tow and equipment and has a way of cutting the towline nearby, and reports how the tow rides and any failure. It is not limited to night or to the engine room.
